observation.visible_scene: A fire burns low on a horizontal log structure against a dark, dimly lit outdoor background (dusk/night) with silhouetted trees and an angled fallen trunk on the right. The camera viewpoint and background elements stay fixed across the excerpt. Bright orange-yellow flames occupy the center, with a glowing ember bed visible beneath the front log.
visible_changes: The flames continuously deform and flicker: tongues of fire rise, merge, split, and change height and shape from frame to frame while remaining anchored at the log base.
The overall flame envelope alternates between taller, narrower columns (e.g., early and mid frames) and shorter, broader, more spread-out bursts, without a single monotonic trend.

Small detached flame fragments/sparks appear briefly above the main flame body in some frames (e.g., around t=0.20, t=0.67, t=2.40) and vanish in others, indicating intermittent upward motion of burning bits.
The glowing base under the front log persists throughout, with its brightness and the spread of low flames along the log shifting slightly but not extinguishing.
No object translation of the logs or background occurs; all apparent motion is flame deformation and the rise of small flame fragments.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the fire looked like before t=0 and how it evolves after t=2.67 (whether it grows, dies, or is tended) is not shown.
The fuel source, ignition cause, and surrounding context beyond the visible log pile are unseen.
Whether the small detached flame bits are sparks, embers, or separate flame tongues is not determinable from the frames.
uncertain_details: Camera motion cannot be fully ruled out, but background positions appear constant, so any movement is negligible/uncertain.
Exact height of individual flame tongues varies frame to frame; the apparent 'tall' vs 'short' phases are sampling of flicker, not a controlled change.
Distinguishing true detachment of a flame fragment from occlusion by a darker flame region is uncertain in several frames.
